change.title: pr-2-flat
change.description: Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Shared BasePaginator now allows negative offsets for prev cursors
findings.body: The base slice previously used `offset` unchanged. Now `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. For `is_prev` cursors a client-supplied negative offset passes straight into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django raises AssertionError on negative slice indexes, which gives a 500. Every paginator that inherits BasePaginator is affected, not only audit logs. The comment claims the queryset handles boundary conditions, and that is false. Cursor offsets come from the `cursor` query parameter. Revert this hunk.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator passes user-controlled negative offset to queryset slice
findings.body: With `enable_advanced_features`, `cursor.offset < 0` gives `queryset[cursor.offset:stop]`. Django does not support negative indexing and raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`, so the request fails with a 500. The comment 'ORM properly handles negative slicing' is wrong. The offset is parsed from the request cursor with no validation (cursors.py:28). If the paginator ever did honor it, it would expose rows outside the normal page bounds. The paginator also duplicates BasePaginator.get_result almost entirely.

findings.title: Undocumented client-toggled paginator path on audit logs, unrelated to the PR's span-buffer work
findings.body: `optimized_pagination=true` switches to a paginator whose only added behavior is the negative-offset path. It is gated by `request.user.is_superuser or member.has_global_access`, a broad gate for an audit-log endpoint. This change has nothing to do with the span-buffer change in the rest of the PR. Remove the endpoint change and OptimizedCursorPaginator. Line 72 and line 89 also have trailing whitespace.

findings.title: Redirect depth limit cut from 10000 to 1000
findings.body: Segment trees deeper than 1000 now fail to join correctly, a tenfold reduction. The removed comment documented the tradeoff. Nothing in the PR explains the change. Spans are silently mis-grouped for deep traces.

findings.title: Segments over 1000 spans are silently truncated, and the earlier size check was removed
findings.body: `zpopmin` drops the oldest spans (lowest end_timestamp) once a set exceeds 1000, with no metric or log. The old behavior in buffer.py was to skip the segment with a `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric and an error log. That check was deleted, and `self.max_segment_spans` is no longer enforced. The hardcoded 1000 ignores that setting. Data is lost silently.

findings.title: Existing Redis sets are incompatible after the sadd to zadd switch
findings.body: Keys already written as plain sets make `zcard`, `zunionstore` and `zscan` fail with WRONGTYPE during a rolling deploy. Also, `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` in factory.py:141 raises KeyError for spans missing the field. Consider a migration plan or `.get` with a fallback.

summary: The PR's negative-offset pagination changes would return 500s for crafted cursors, since Django rejects negative slice indexes. They also add an unrelated, client-toggled paginator path to the audit-log endpoint. The span buffer switch to sorted sets silently truncates segments over 1000 spans. It also cuts the redirect depth limit tenfold and drops the span-count error log and metric. I did not read the span buffer code in full; I judged it from the diff.
